entries.meaning: I revere the beneficent Brahmin lineage, dear to King Rāma and dispeller of blemish: it is the root of the tree of dharma, a bliss-giving full moon to the ocean of discernment, the sun for the lotus of detachment, the remover of sin's dense darkness and of suffering, and like the sky-born wind when masses of delusion-clouds must be torn apart.
entries.note: Original close English rendering from the pinned Devanagari witness; editorial work awaiting independent review. The syntactically compressed image svah-sambhavam is read contextually as the sky-born wind.

words: of the tree of dharma; of the ocean of discernment
the sun for the lotus of detachment
in the work of tearing apart masses of delusion-clouds

entries.meaning: I worship the enchanting Rāma as he walks the path with Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa: his form has the beauty of a dense cloud of bliss, he wears lovely yellow cloth, bears bow and arrow in his hand and the weight of a splendid quiver at his waist, has long lotus eyes, and shines beneath a mass of matted locks.
entries.note: Original close English rendering from the pinned Devanagari witness; editorial work awaiting independent review.

words: whose form has the beauty of a dense cloud of bliss
bearing at his waist the weight of a shining quiver
with a mass of matted locks worn

entries.meaning: Umā, Rāma's virtues are profound: learned sages find detachment in them, while the utterly foolish—those turned away from Hari and without love of dharma—find delusion.
entries.note: Original close English rendering of the pinned Awadhi reading; editorial work awaiting independent review.
